title: Which Rooms Should Have Carpet? A Room-by-Room Guide for Sammamish Homes
meta: Carpet belongs in Sammamish bedrooms, upstairs halls, bonus rooms and stairs, not kitchens, baths or entries. Wills Flooring's room-by-room guide says why.
keywords: which rooms should have carpet, carpet in bedrooms vs hardwood, should stairs be carpeted, carpet in living room or not, carpet installation Sammamish WA, best flooring for each room

blocks.lead: In a Sammamish home, carpet belongs in the bedrooms, the upstairs hallway, the bonus room, the stairs and any finished basement or media room. Keep it out of the kitchen, bathrooms, laundry, mudroom and main entry.
blocks.detail: That split matches how plateau families live: hard floors where mud, water and dogs arrive, soft floors where people sleep and watch movies. The main-floor living room is the one real judgment call.

blocks.html: Most of the houses we visit in Klahanie, Trossachs and around Pine Lake were built between 1995 and 2012 with builder carpet nearly everywhere except the kitchen. Fifteen years, two kids and a Labrador later, the owners know that layout was wrong but are not sure which rooms should keep carpet. This guide goes room by room. For service details, see our carpet installation page.

head: Room
Carpet?
Why, and what to use instead
rows: Warmth underfoot at 6 am, quiet, and a soft landing for kids. A dense nylon or triexta plush is the standard pick.
It connects carpeted rooms and takes the same traffic as the stairs. Use the same carpet so the run is continuous.
Carpet grips better than any hard surface for kids and older dogs. Use a low, dense pile and wrap the nosings tightly.
Cold floor, big open space, toys and screens. Carpet with a thick pad fixes the cold and the echo at once.
Sound absorption and warmth matter most here. A moisture-barrier pad is non-negotiable on any slab.
Open plans that flow into the kitchen want one hard floor throughout. A closed living room can still take carpet.
Chairs, spills and crumbs. Hard flooring plus a rug is easier to live with and to sell.
Water, grease and cleaning chemicals. Vinyl plank or tile.
This is where Sammamish mud and wet dogs land. Nothing soft survives it.
blocks.note: Two-story homes in Sahalee and Beaver Lake often settle on a clean rule: hard floors downstairs, carpet upstairs.

blocks.text: Why bedrooms and the upstairs still want carpet in 2026

items.title: Warmth where you are barefoot
items.text: Sammamish bedrooms sit over garages, crawlspaces or open ceilings, and the plateau runs colder than Seattle. Carpet and pad insulate better than any hard floor, which is what people notice when they switch a bedroom to plank and regret it by November.

items.title: Quiet between floors
items.text: Carpet upstairs is the biggest thing keeping footsteps, dropped toys and early-morning dog nails from reaching the main floor. Families who put hard flooring in upstairs bedrooms almost always add rugs back within a year.

items.title: Soft landings
items.text: Toddlers, kids wrestling on the floor and older relatives all fall more safely on carpet. Stairs are the clearest case: a carpeted stair with a dense pile is the safest stair in the house.

items.title: The budget goes further upstairs
items.text: Bedrooms are large, low-traffic rooms that do not need premium flooring to look good. Carpet there, with the hard-surface budget saved for the main floor, is how most plateau remodels come out looking finished.

blocks.text: Price your Sammamish carpet project room by room

blocks.html: Choosing room by room has a price consequence. Carpet labor is $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in over pad with a 500 sq ft minimum, so a single 12 by 14 bedroom of 168 sq ft still bills 500 × $0.99 = $495. Do the upstairs at once and that minimum disappears into the job: bedrooms, hall and 14 steps at about 950 sq ft is 950 × $0.99 + 14 × $30 = $1,360.50 in labor. Glue-down over a basement slab is $1.29 per sq ft, old carpet out $0.45 and furniture $0.25, with carpet and pad quoted at the estimate.

blocks.note: Labor only, with the 500 sq ft minimum applied. Carpet and pad are quoted at the estimate.

blocks.text: Stairs, bonus rooms and basements: the judgment calls

items.text: Carpet is right for most Sammamish families, but only in a low, dense cut pile or a tight loop. Thick plush over a nosing wears through at the edge. If the staircase is visible from the entry, hardwood treads with a carpet runner give you looks and grip.
items.note: Ask for wrapped nosings and a firm pad on the treads

items.text: The room over the garage in a Klahanie or Trossachs two-story is the coldest room in the house. Carpet with a thicker, denser pad solves that and makes it usable as a playroom.
items.note: If it doubles as a gym, consider carpet tiles so a damaged section can be swapped

items.text: Carpet wins for sound and comfort, but only after the slab passes a moisture test. Carpet over a damp slab is the most common flooring failure we see on the plateau.
items.note: Use a pad with a built-in moisture barrier and keep a dehumidifier in the plan

blocks.text: Rooms where carpet is a mistake in a Sammamish house

a.title: Keep or install carpet when
items: The room is a bedroom, upstairs hall, stair run or bonus room
You want the floor warm and quiet more than washable
Kids or older dogs use the space daily
The subfloor is wood, or a slab that tests dry

b.title: Skip carpet when
items: The room opens directly to the kitchen in one continuous space
Wet dogs, boots and bikes come through the door
There is any history of a slab leak or a damp crawlspace
Someone has severe dust allergies and will not vacuum weekly

blocks.title: The open-plan trap:
blocks.text: Many 2000s plateau homes have a family room that flows into the kitchen with no doorway. Carpeting it puts a soft edge two steps from the stove and the dog bowl: it stains first and sells worst. Run one hard floor through the space and add a large rug.
Mistakes we see on the plateau

items.html: Carpeting everything because the builder did. Builder-grade carpet in a dining room or entry was a cost decision, not a design one.
Ripping carpet out of every upstairs bedroom to modernize. Cold, echoing bedrooms are the most common regret we hear at follow-up visits.
Ignoring the pad. A dense, thinner pad on stairs and a thicker pad in bedrooms is the right pairing. One pad for the whole house is how stairs get spongy.
Carpeting a basement without a moisture test. Sammamish sits on clay and glacial till, and a basement that has looked dry for years can still wick moisture. Read our basement carpet guide first.

blocks.text: Checklist before you decide room by room

items.html: Walk the house with the daily routine in mind. Where do wet dogs, sports bags and groceries enter? Those rooms go hard-surface.
Draw the main-floor sightlines. Rooms visible from each other without a door should share one floor. Closed rooms can differ.
Match fiber to the room. Nylon or triexta on stairs and halls, softer polyester or triexta in low-traffic bedrooms. Our fiber guide explains the trade-offs.
Test any slab and check the crawlspace. We meter subfloors at the free estimate, and a high reading changes the plan for that room.
Think about the next owner. Sammamish buyers expect hard floors on the main level and are happy with good carpet upstairs.

faq.q: Should bedrooms have carpet or hardwood?
faq.a: For most Sammamish families, carpet. Bedrooms are where warmth, quiet and a soft floor matter most and where spills and mud matter least. Hardwood or plank in bedrooms looks clean in photos but usually ends up under rugs within a year, especially over a garage.

faq.q: Is it better to carpet stairs or leave them hardwood?
faq.a: Carpet grips better and is safer for kids, older adults and dogs, at $30 per step. If the staircase is a feature you see from the front door, hardwood treads with a carpet runner give you the look plus the grip. Keep the pile low and dense either way.

faq.q: Can I carpet the living room if it opens to the kitchen?
faq.a: We advise against it. An open plan reads as one room, and a carpet edge two steps from the stove stains first and looks chopped up to buyers. Run a hard floor through the connected space and add a large rug where the sofa sits.

faq.q: Is carpet in a basement a bad idea in Sammamish?
faq.a: Not if the slab tests dry and you use a pad with a moisture barrier, or glue the carpet down at $1.29 per sq ft. The plateau's clay soils mean many basements carry moisture through the concrete even when they look dry. We meter the slab at the estimate.

faq.q: Does carpet hurt resale value in Sammamish?
faq.a: Only where buyers expect hard floors: kitchen, entry, dining and an open main living area. Good-condition carpet in bedrooms, halls, bonus rooms and stairs is what most Sammamish buyers expect and is not a negative. Worn or stained carpet anywhere is.

faq.q: What does it cost to carpet just the bedrooms and stairs?
faq.a: Labor is published: $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in and $30 per step, with a 500 sq ft minimum. A typical Klahanie upstairs of 950 sq ft with 14 steps is $1,360.50 in labor, plus $0.45 per sq ft to remove the old carpet. Carpet and pad are quoted at the estimate.
